sections.subtopic: Foot of Perpendicular, Image and Reflection
sections.title: Foot, image and reflection

board_events.text: Foot, Image & Reflection
Shine a torch straight at a wall: where the beam hits perpendicularly is the foot of the perpendicular.

board_events.caption: The foot Q is the midpoint of P and its image P-prime.
board_events.svg: <svg font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" viewBox="0 0 420 260" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><line x1="60" y1="60" x2="360" y2="200" stroke="#059669" stroke-width="2"/><text x="330" y="196" font-size="11" fill="#059669">mirror line</text><circle cx="180" cy="40" r="4" fill="#c026d3"/><text x="160" y="36" font-size="12" fill="#c026d3">P</text><circle cx="151" cy="102" r="4" fill="#333"/><text x="128" y="100" font-size="11" fill="#333">Q</text><circle cx="122" cy="165" r="4" fill="#1a56db"/><text x="128" y="178" font-size="12" fill="#1a56db">P′ (image)</text><line x1="180" y1="40" x2="122" y2="165" stroke="#c026d3" stroke-width="1.3" stroke-dasharray="4 3"/><text x="188" y="74" font-size="11" fill="#666">d</text><text x="146" y="140" font-size="11" fill="#666">d</text></svg>

board_events.text: Walk an equal distance past the wall and you reach the image — as far behind as $P$ is in front.
So the foot is halfway to the image; the image is twice as far as the foot.
The line $ax+by+c=0$ has normal direction $(a,b)$; you step from $P$ along it to land on the line.
One step reaches the foot; two steps reach the mirror image.

segments.text: This last subtopic is really one picture, turned into formulas. Let's set the picture up.

Stand at a point P and shine a torch straight at a wall, and let the wall be our line. The spot where the beam hits perpendicularly is the foot of the perpendicular — the closest point on the line to P.
Look at the diagram: P above the line, the foot Q on the line, and the image P-prime on the far side. Notice Q sits exactly halfway between P and P-prime.
Now walk an equal distance past the wall along that same beam, and you reach the image — exactly as far behind the mirror as you stand in front, just like your reflection in glass.
So two facts fall out at once: the foot is halfway to the image, and the image is twice as far as the foot.
How do we get there algebraically? The line has normal direction a comma b, and you step from P straight along that normal until you land on the line.
The size of that step is governed by a x one plus b y one plus c, over a squared plus b squared — the very expression that measured distance earlier, now reused as a step size.
And the whole subtopic is just: take one step to reach the foot, and two steps to reach the mirror image.
यह आख़िरी subtopic असल में एक ही picture है, formulas में बदली हुई। picture set करते हैं।
एक point P पर खड़े हो और एक wall पर सीधे torch मारो, wall को हमारी line मान लो। जहाँ beam perpendicularly टकराती है वो foot of the perpendicular है — line पर P का सबसे नज़दीकी point।
Diagram देखो: line के ऊपर P, line पर foot Q, और दूसरी तरफ़ image P-prime। ध्यान दो Q ठीक P और P-prime के बीचोंबीच बैठा है।
अब उसी beam के साथ wall के पार बराबर distance चलो, और तुम image पर पहुँच जाते हो — mirror के पीछे उतना ही दूर जितना तुम आगे खड़े हो, बिल्कुल glass में reflection की तरह।
तो दो facts एक साथ निकल आते हैं: foot image तक आधा रास्ता है, और image foot से twice दूर है।
Algebraically वहाँ कैसे पहुँचें? Line की normal direction a comma b है, और तुम P से उस normal के साथ सीधे step करते हो जब तक line पर न पहुँच जाओ।
उस step का size a x one plus b y one plus c, over a squared plus b squared से तय होता है — वही expression जो पहले distance नापता था, अब step size की तरह reuse।
और पूरा subtopic बस इतना है: foot तक एक step, और mirror image तक दो steps।

sections.subtopic: Foot of Perpendicular, Image and Reflection
sections.title: Proof: the foot of the perpendicular

board_events.text: Proof: Foot of the Perpendicular
The segment $PQ$ is perpendicular to the line, so it points along the normal $(a,b)$.

board_events.caption: Q = P + t(a,b), with t chosen so Q lands on the line.
board_events.svg: <svg font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" viewBox="0 0 400 240" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><line x1="60" y1="180" x2="360" y2="80" stroke="#059669" stroke-width="2"/><text x="330" y="76" font-size="11" fill="#059669">line</text><circle cx="150" cy="50" r="4" fill="#c026d3"/><text x="130" y="46" font-size="12" fill="#c026d3">P</text><circle cx="180" cy="140" r="4" fill="#333"/><text x="186" y="140" font-size="11" fill="#333">Q</text><line x1="150" y1="50" x2="180" y2="140" stroke="#c026d3" stroke-width="1.4" stroke-dasharray="4 3"/><text x="188" y="98" font-size="10" fill="#666">step t (a, b)</text></svg>

board_events.text: Since $Q$ lies on the line, substitute and solve for the scalar $t$.

segments.text: Let's derive the foot formula — it is a single clean idea about stepping along the normal.
The segment from P to the foot Q is perpendicular to the line, which means it points exactly along the line's normal direction, a comma b.
So Q is reached from P by stepping some scalar amount t along that normal, as the diagram shows.
That is, Q equals x one plus t a, and y one plus t b.
But Q also lies on the line, so plug those coordinates into the line's equation and solve for the one unknown t.
Substituting gives a times x one plus t a, plus b times y one plus t b, plus c, equals zero.
Grouping the t terms and rearranging, t comes out as minus a x one plus b y one plus c, over a squared plus b squared.
Feed that t back in, and the foot satisfies x minus x one over a, equals y minus y one over b, equals that same step — the compact foot formula.
चलो foot formula derive करें — यह normal के साथ step करने का एक clean idea है।
P से foot Q तक का segment line के perpendicular है, यानी वो line की normal direction, a comma b, के साथ ठीक point करता है।
तो Q, P से उस normal के साथ कुछ scalar amount t step करके मिलता है, जैसा diagram दिखाता है।
यानी Q बराबर x one plus t a, और y one plus t b।
पर Q line पर भी है, तो वो coordinates line की equation में डालो और एक unknown t के लिए solve करो।
Substitute करने पर मिलता है a times x one plus t a, plus b times y one plus t b, plus c, बराबर zero।
t terms group करके rearrange करो, तो t निकलता है minus a x one plus b y one plus c, over a squared plus b squared।
वो t वापस डालो, और foot satisfy करता है x minus x one over a, बराबर y minus y one over b, बराबर वही step — compact foot formula।

sections.subtopic: Foot of Perpendicular, Image and Reflection
sections.title: Proof: image of a point, and reflecting a line

board_events.text: Proof: Image of a Point, Reflecting a Line
The foot $Q$ is the midpoint of $P$ and its image $P'$, so $P' = 2Q - P$.
So the image uses parameter $2t$ — exactly double the foot's step.
To reflect a whole line $m$ in a line $\ell$: reflect two of its points and rejoin them.
Shortcut: if $m$ and $\ell$ intersect, the reflection also passes through $m \cap \ell$.
So one image point plus that intersection is enough — half the work.

segments.text: Now the image formula, which follows from the foot in one step, plus how to reflect a whole line.
The foot Q is the midpoint of P and its image P-prime. So P-prime equals two Q minus P — just the midpoint relation rearranged.
Substitute Q as P plus t times a comma b, and P-prime becomes P plus two t times a comma b.
So the image uses the parameter two t, exactly double the foot's step. That is the only change from the foot formula.
In coordinates, x-prime minus x one over a equals y-prime minus y one over b equals minus two times a x one plus b y one plus c, over a squared plus b squared.
To reflect a whole line m in a mirror line ell, you cannot tweak the equation directly — instead reflect two of its points and join the images.
There is a neat shortcut: if m and the mirror ell actually intersect, the reflected line also passes through their point of intersection.
So one image point, plus that intersection, is enough to fix the reflected line — which halves the work versus reflecting two separate points.
अब image formula, जो foot से एक ही step में निकलता है, और साथ में पूरी line reflect करने का तरीक़ा।
Foot Q, P और उसके image P-prime का midpoint है। तो P-prime बराबर two Q minus P — बस midpoint relation rearrange किया।
Q को P plus t times a comma b substitute करो, और P-prime बन जाता है P plus two t times a comma b।
तो image parameter two t use करता है, foot के step का ठीक double। foot formula से बस यही change है।
Coordinates में, x-prime minus x one over a बराबर y-prime minus y one over b बराबर minus two times a x one plus b y one plus c, over a squared plus b squared।
किसी mirror line ell में पूरी line m reflect करने के लिए, तुम equation को सीधे tweak नहीं कर सकते — बल्कि उसके दो points reflect करो और images को join करो।
एक neat shortcut है: अगर m और mirror ell सचमुच intersect करें, तो reflected line उनके intersection point से भी गुज़रती है।
तो एक image point, plus वो intersection, reflected line fix करने के लिए काफ़ी है — जो दो अलग points reflect करने के मुक़ाबले काम आधा कर देता है।

sections.subtopic: Foot of Perpendicular, Image and Reflection
sections.title: Foot, image and reflection: formula toolkit

board_events.text: Foot, Image & Reflection — Toolkit
The foot is the midpoint of the point and its image.
Reflect a line: reflect two of its points, then rejoin.
Denominator here is $a^2 + b^2$ — no square root, unlike the distance formula.

segments.text: Here is the whole toolkit for feet, images and reflections.
The foot: x minus x one over a equals y minus y one over b equals minus a x one plus b y one plus c, over a squared plus b squared.
The image is the same, with a factor of two on that numerator — twice the step.
And the anchor relating them: the foot is the midpoint of the point and its image.
For the special mirror y equals x, just swap the coordinates.
For the x-axis, negate the y-coordinate.
For the y-axis, negate the x-coordinate.
To reflect a whole line, reflect two of its points and rejoin them.
One thing to burn in: the denominator here is a squared plus b squared, with no square root — unlike the distance formula, which does take the root. Mixing them is a classic slip.
यह रहा feet, images और reflections का पूरा toolkit।
Foot: x minus x one over a बराबर y minus y one over b बराबर minus a x one plus b y one plus c, over a squared plus b squared।
Image वही है, उस numerator पर factor of two के साथ — twice the step।
और उन्हें जोड़ने वाला anchor: foot, point और उसके image का midpoint है।
Special mirror y बराबर x के लिए, बस coordinates swap करो।
x-axis के लिए, y-coordinate negate करो।
y-axis के लिए, x-coordinate negate करो।
पूरी line reflect करने के लिए, उसके दो points reflect करो और rejoin करो।
एक बात पक्की कर लो: यहाँ denominator है a squared plus b squared, बिना square root के — distance formula के उलट, जो root लेता है। इन्हें mix करना classic slip है।

sections.subtopic: Foot of Perpendicular, Image and Reflection
sections.title: Worked examples: foot, and image in y = x

board_events.text: Worked: Foot & Image in $y = x$
Example 1: foot of the perpendicular from $P(2,3)$ to $x + y - 1 = 0$.
Example 2: image of $(4,-1)$ in the line $y = x$.
$y = x$ is a special mirror — just swap the coordinates.
Recognise $y=x$, the $x$-axis, and the $y$-axis on sight, and use swap or negate.

segments.text: Two examples: a foot by the general formula, then an image by the fast special-mirror trick.
Example one: find the foot of the perpendicular from P at two, three to the line x plus y minus one equals zero.
Here a and b are both one, and c is minus one. So a x one plus b y one plus c is two plus three minus one, that is four; a squared plus b squared is two; so the step t is minus two.
Then Q is two plus t times one, and three plus t times one, which is zero comma one — the foot.
Example two: find the image of four comma minus one in the line y equals x.
Do not grind the general formula here — y equals x is a special mirror, so you simply swap the two coordinates.
Swapping gives minus one comma four. Done in one move.
So train your eye: the moment you see y equals x, the x-axis, or the y-axis, reach for swap or negate rather than the full machinery.
दो examples: general formula से एक foot, फिर fast special-mirror trick से एक image।
Example one: P at two, three से line x plus y minus one बराबर zero तक perpendicular का foot ढूँढो।
यहाँ a और b दोनों one हैं, और c है minus one। तो a x one plus b y one plus c है two plus three minus one, यानी four; a squared plus b squared है two; तो step t है minus two।
फिर Q है two plus t times one, और three plus t times one, यानी zero comma one — foot।
Example two: four comma minus one का line y बराबर x में image ढूँढो।
यहाँ general formula मत घिसो — y बराबर x एक special mirror है, तो बस दोनों coordinates swap कर दो।
Swap करने पर मिलता है minus one comma four। एक ही move में हो गया।
तो अपनी नज़र train करो: जैसे ही y बराबर x, x-axis, या y-axis दिखे, पूरी machinery की जगह swap या negate उठाओ।

sections.subtopic: Foot of Perpendicular, Image and Reflection
sections.title: Worked example: image, and verifying equal distances

board_events.text: Worked: Image & Verifying Equal Distances
Find the image of $P(1,1)$ in the line $3x - 4y + 5 = 0$.
Distance of $P$ from the line is $\tfrac{|4|}{5} = 0.8$.
Equal distances, opposite sides — exactly what a mirror image must satisfy.

segments.text: This example finds an image and then checks it, so you learn to trust your own answer.
Find the image of P at one, one in the line three x minus four y plus five equals zero.
Compute a x one plus b y one plus c: three minus four plus five, which is four; and a squared plus b squared is twenty five.
The image step is minus two times four over twenty five, that is minus eight over twenty five.
So P-prime is one minus twenty four over twenty five, and one plus thirty two over twenty five, which is one over twenty five, comma fifty seven over twenty five.
Now verify. The distance of P from the line is the modulus of four over five, that is zero point eight.
Plug P-prime into the distance formula and it also comes out to four over five, zero point eight.
Equal distances on opposite sides of the line — which is exactly the defining property of a mirror image. The check confirms the answer.
यह example एक image ढूँढता है और फिर उसे check करता है, ताकि तुम अपने answer पर भरोसा करना सीखो।
P at one, one का line three x minus four y plus five बराबर zero में image ढूँढो।
a x one plus b y one plus c निकालो: three minus four plus five, यानी four; और a squared plus b squared है twenty five।
Image step है minus two times four over twenty five, यानी minus eight over twenty five।
तो P-prime है one minus twenty four over twenty five, और one plus thirty two over twenty five, यानी one over twenty five, comma fifty seven over twenty five।
अब verify करो। line से P की distance है modulus of four over five, यानी zero point eight।
P-prime को distance formula में डालो तो वो भी four over five, zero point eight आता है।
Line के opposite sides पर equal distances — यही तो mirror image की defining property है। Check answer की पुष्टि कर देता है।

sections.subtopic: Foot of Perpendicular, Image and Reflection
sections.title: Worked example: reflected ray (advanced)

board_events.text: Worked: Reflected Ray (Advanced)
A ray along $x - 2y + 5 = 0$ strikes the mirror $3x - 4y + 4 = 0$. Find the reflected ray.
Incidence point $I$: solve the two lines together.
Take $A(-5,0)$ on the incident ray and reflect it in the mirror.

segments.text: <curious>Here is the Advanced payoff — reflection turns an optics problem into two coordinate computations.</curious>
A ray of light travelling along x minus two y plus five equals zero strikes the mirror three x minus four y plus four equals zero. Find the reflected ray.
The reflected ray passes through the incidence point, so first find where the incident ray meets the mirror by solving the two lines together.
That intersection is the point I, at six comma eleven halves.
Now take any convenient point on the incident ray — say A at minus five, zero — and reflect it in the mirror using the image formula.
Here a A x plus b A y plus c is minus fifteen plus four, that is minus eleven, and the image step works out to twenty two over twenty five.
That sends A to its image A-prime, at minus fifty nine over twenty five, comma minus eighty eight over twenty five.

The reflected ray is simply the line joining I and A-prime, and working out its equation gives forty one x minus thirty eight y minus thirty seven equals zero. Two coordinate steps, and the optics is done.
<curious>यह रहा Advanced payoff — reflection एक optics problem को दो coordinate computations में बदल देता है।</curious>
x minus two y plus five बराबर zero के साथ चलती light की एक ray, mirror three x minus four y plus four बराबर zero से टकराती है। Reflected ray ढूँढो।
Reflected ray incidence point से गुज़रती है, तो पहले incident ray और mirror का मिलना ढूँढो, दोनों lines को साथ solve करके।
वो intersection है point I, six comma eleven halves पर।
अब incident ray पर कोई convenient point लो — जैसे A at minus five, zero — और उसे image formula से mirror में reflect करो।
यहाँ a A x plus b A y plus c है minus fifteen plus four, यानी minus eleven, और image step निकलता है twenty two over twenty five।
यह A को उसके image A-prime पर भेजता है, minus fifty nine over twenty five, comma minus eighty eight over twenty five।
Reflected ray बस I और A-prime को जोड़ने वाली line है, और उसकी equation निकालने पर मिलता है forty one x minus thirty eight y minus thirty seven बराबर zero। दो coordinate steps, और optics हो गया।

sections.subtopic: Foot of Perpendicular, Image and Reflection
sections.title: Pitfalls and pro-tips: foot, image and reflection

board_events.text: Pitfalls: Foot, Image & Reflection
Foot uses the step $-\tfrac{ax_1+by_1+c}{a^2+b^2}$; the image uses twice that — do not drop the $2$.
For $y=x$, the $x$-axis, and the $y$-axis, use swap or negate — faster and error-proof.
You cannot reflect an equation directly (except in $y=x$); reflect points instead.
Denominator here is $a^2+b^2$, no root — contrast with the distance formula's $\sqrt{a^2+b^2}$.
Pro-tip: reflecting a line? One image point plus the mirror intersection is enough.
That halves the work versus reflecting two separate points.
One step to the foot, two steps to the mirror — keep the factor of two straight.

segments.text: Let's close the last subtopic with its four traps.
Trap one: the foot uses the single step, but the image uses twice that step. Drop the factor of two and you land right on the line instead of behind it.
Trap two: for the special mirrors — y equals x, the x-axis, and the y-axis — use swap or negate. It is faster and essentially error-proof.
Trap three: you cannot reflect an equation by tweaking its coefficients, except for the y equals x case where swapping x and y works. In general, reflect points instead.
Trap four: the denominator in these formulas is a squared plus b squared, with no square root, which contrasts with the distance formula's root of a squared plus b squared. Mixing them is common.
<whisper>And the pro-tip for reflecting a line: when the line meets the mirror, one image point plus that intersection pins down the reflected line.</whisper>
That halves the work compared with reflecting two separate points and joining them.
Sum it up as one line: one step to the foot, two steps to the mirror — keep that factor of two straight and this subtopic is yours.
आख़िरी subtopic को उसके चार traps के साथ बंद करते हैं।
Trap one: foot single step use करता है, पर image उसका twice। factor of two छोड़ा तो तुम line के पीछे नहीं, line पर ही आ गिरते हो।
Trap two: special mirrors — y बराबर x, x-axis, और y-axis — के लिए swap या negate use करो। यह faster और लगभग error-proof है।
Trap three: तुम equation को उसके coefficients tweak करके reflect नहीं कर सकते, सिवाय y बराबर x case के जहाँ x और y swap करना काम करता है। आमतौर पर points reflect करो।
Trap four: इन formulas में denominator है a squared plus b squared, बिना square root, जो distance formula के root of a squared plus b squared से उलट है। इन्हें mix करना common है।
<whisper>और line reflect करने का pro-tip: जब line mirror से मिले, तो एक image point plus वो intersection reflected line pin कर देते हैं।</whisper>
यह दो अलग points reflect करके जोड़ने के मुक़ाबले काम आधा कर देता है।
इसे एक line में समेटो: foot तक एक step, mirror तक दो steps — वो factor of two सीधा रखो और यह subtopic तुम्हारा है।

sections.title: Formula recap I: points, slope, equations

board_events.text: Formula Recap I: Points, Slope, Equations
Your complete toolkit through Equations of a Line — restated, not re-taught.

segments.text: We have covered the whole chapter; here is your complete toolkit for the first half, restated in one place.
Distance between two points is the root of the squared coordinate differences.
The internal section point cross-weights the coordinates over m plus n; the centroid averages all three vertices over three.
The triangle area is one half the modulus of that cyclic expression, and it is zero exactly when the points are collinear.
Slope is tan of the inclination, or the two-point ratio; equal slopes mean parallel, and a product of minus one means perpendicular.
The angle between two lines is the inverse tangent of the modulus of that slope expression.
For equations, keep point-slope, intercept form, and slope-intercept ready to hand.
And the normal form and general form round it out, with slope minus A over B from the general form.
That is your complete toolkit through Equations of a Line — restated for quick recall, not taught again.
हमने पूरा chapter cover कर लिया; यह रहा पहले half का पूरा toolkit, एक जगह restated।
दो points के बीच distance squared coordinate differences का root है।
Internal section point coordinates को m plus n over cross-weight करता है; centroid तीनों vertices को three over average करता है।
Triangle area उस cyclic expression के modulus का one half है, और zero तभी जब points collinear हों।
Slope inclination का tan है, या two-point ratio; equal slopes मतलब parallel, और product minus one मतलब perpendicular।
दो lines के बीच angle उस slope expression के modulus का inverse tangent है।
Equations के लिए, point-slope, intercept form, और slope-intercept हाथ में रखो।
और normal form तथा general form इसे पूरा करते हैं, general form से slope minus A over B के साथ।
यह Equations of a Line तक तुम्हारा पूरा toolkit है — quick recall के लिए restated, फिर से पढ़ाया नहीं।

sections.title: Formula recap II: distance, family, bisectors, reflection

board_events.text: Formula Recap II: Distance, Family, Bisectors, Reflection

board_events.latex: \begin{vmatrix} a_1 & b_1 & c_1 \\ a_2 & b_2 & c_2 \\ a_3 & b_3 & c_3 \end{vmatrix} = 0;\quad L_1 + \lambda L_2 = 0

board_events.text: Complete toolkit for the back half — your one-glance revision board.

segments.text: And here is the toolkit for the second half of the chapter, all on one board.
Point-to-line distance divides by the root of A squared plus B squared; parallel-line distance is the constant difference over the same root, after normalizing.
The symmetric form gives the signed distance r directly along the inclination theta.
Cramer's rule gives the intersection point of two lines in one shot.
Concurrency is the vanishing three by three determinant, and the family through a junction is L one plus lambda L two equals zero.
The angle bisectors set the two normalized expressions equal, with a plus or minus.
The foot of the perpendicular steps once along the normal, over a squared plus b squared with no root.
And the image steps twice — the same formula with a factor of two on the numerator.
That completes your one-glance revision board for the back half of Straight Lines.
और यह रहा chapter के दूसरे half का toolkit, सब एक board पर।
Point-to-line distance root of A squared plus B squared से divide करती है; parallel-line distance normalize करने के बाद उसी root over constant difference है।
Symmetric form signed distance r को सीधे inclination theta के साथ देता है।
Cramer's rule दो lines का intersection point एक ही बार में देता है।
Concurrency vanishing three by three determinant है, और junction से family L one plus lambda L two बराबर zero।
Angle bisectors दो normalized expressions को बराबर रखते हैं, plus या minus के साथ।
Foot of the perpendicular normal के साथ एक बार step करता है, over a squared plus b squared, बिना root।
और image दो बार step करता है — वही formula numerator पर factor of two के साथ।
यह Straight Lines के दूसरे half के लिए तुम्हारा one-glance revision board पूरा करता है।

board_events.text: Cheat Sheet: One-Line Memory Aids
'Internal adds, external subtracts' — the $m \pm n$ denominator.
'Area zero means in a row' — collinearity.
'Horizontal Zero, Vertical Void' — slope $0$ versus undefined.
'Flip and Negate' for perpendicular slopes; 'equally inclined $\Rightarrow \pm 1$'.
'Minus A over B' for slope from the general form; '$p$ is positive, period'.
'Normalize, then subtract' for parallel lines; 'modulus on top, root-sum-squares below'.
'Both zero $\Rightarrow$ sum zero' (family); 'determinant dies $\Rightarrow$ they meet'.
'Positive constants first, then plus is the origin's side'; 'one step to the foot, two to the mirror'.

segments.text: <excited>You have reached the end of Straight Lines — here is the whole chapter as a handful of memory hooks.</excited>
For the section formula: internal adds, external subtracts — that is the m plus or minus n in the denominator.
For collinearity: area zero means in a row.
For slope poles: horizontal zero, vertical void — slope zero for horizontal, undefined for vertical.
For perpendiculars: flip and negate; and a line equally inclined to the axes has slope plus or minus one.
From the general form: minus A over B for the slope; and in the normal form, p is positive, period.
For parallel lines: normalize, then subtract; and remember, modulus on top, root-sum-of-squares below.
For the family trick: both zero implies the sum is zero; and for concurrency, the determinant dies, so they meet.

And for the last two subtopics: positive constants first, then plus is the origin's side; and one step to the foot, two steps to the mirror. That is the entire chapter in your pocket — revise from these anchors.
<excited>तुम Straight Lines के अंत तक पहुँच गए — यह रहा पूरा chapter कुछ memory hooks के रूप में।</excited>
Section formula के लिए: internal adds, external subtracts — यही denominator में m plus या minus n है।
Collinearity के लिए: area zero means in a row।
Slope poles के लिए: horizontal zero, vertical void — horizontal के लिए slope zero, vertical के लिए undefined।
Perpendiculars के लिए: flip and negate; और axes से equally inclined line की slope plus या minus one।
General form से: slope के लिए minus A over B; और normal form में, p is positive, period।
Parallel lines के लिए: normalize, then subtract; और याद रखो, modulus on top, root-sum-of-squares below।
Family trick के लिए: both zero मतलब sum zero; और concurrency के लिए, determinant dies, तो they meet।

और आख़िरी दो subtopics के लिए: positive constants first, then plus is the origin's side; और one step to the foot, two steps to the mirror। यह पूरा chapter तुम्हारी जेब में — इन्हीं anchors से revise करो।
